title: Afghan biscuits (chocolate cornflake cookies)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and line two trays with baking paper.
Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, then stir in the flour and cocoa.
Gently fold in the cornflakes, trying not to crush them too much.
Spoon the mixture into 14 heaped mounds on the trays and press down lightly.
Bake for 15 minutes, then cool on the trays.
Mix the icing sugar, cocoa and hot water into a thick, glossy icing, spoon it onto each biscuit and top with a walnut half.

title: Boil up (Māori pork bone and greens soup with doughboys)
steps: Put the pork bones in a large pot with the water and onion, bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Add the kūmara or potatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, rub the butter into the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt, then stir in enough milk to make a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough into the simmering soup, add the cabbage, cover, and cook for 10 to 12 minutes until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through.
Stir in the greens, cook for 2 minutes until wilted, and season with salt.
Serve in deep bowls with some bone or meat in each, ideally with buttered bread.

title: Cheese roll (Southland-style toasted cheese roll)

ingredients.name: soft white sandwich bread, crusts removed
sweet chilli sauce or tomato sauce, to serve

steps: Mix the cheese, onion, evaporated milk and mustard powder into a thick, spreadable paste.
Flatten each slice of bread with a rolling pin so it is thin and pliable.
Spread a generous layer of the cheese mixture across each slice, leaving a thin border.
Roll each slice up tightly and place seam-side down on a baking tray.
Brush the rolls generously with melted butter and grill or bake at 220 C for 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Serve hot with sweet chilli sauce or tomato sauce.

title: Colonial goose (stuffed roast lamb leg)
steps: Soften the onion in 1 tbsp of the butter, then mix it with the breadcrumbs, sage, parsley, egg, salt and pepper to make the stuffing.
Open out the lamb, season it on the inside, and spread the stuffing evenly over it.
Roll the lamb up and tie it securely with kitchen string at 3 cm intervals.
Rub the outside with the remaining butter, season, and place in a roasting tin with a splash of stock.
Roast at 200 C for 20 minutes, then at 160 C for 1 hour 30 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads at least 70 C for well done. Rest under foil for 15 minutes.
Make a gravy by stirring the flour into the pan juices, adding the remaining stock, and simmering until thickened. Slice the lamb and serve.

title: Ginger crunch (iced ginger shortbread slice)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Cream the butter and sugar, then mix in the flour, baking powder and ginger to a crumbly dough, and press it firmly into the tin.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden, then leave it to cool for 5 minutes.
Melt the icing butter with the golden syrup, then stir in the icing sugar and ginger until smooth.
Pour the icing over the warm base, spreading it evenly, and let it set.
Cut into fingers while the base is still slightly warm, then cool completely before lifting out.

title: Hāngī (Māori earth-oven feast, steamed in the home oven)

ingredients.name: pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
kūmara (or sweet potato), in large pieces
clean cloths or paper towels and foil

steps: Season the pork and chicken with salt and pepper and arrange them in a deep roasting tin lined with a large sheet of foil.
Place the onions among the meat and add the kūmara, potatoes and pumpkin on top, with the cabbage last.
Soak clean cloths or paper towels in water, wring them out, and lay them over the vegetables so they trap steam, then seal the foil tightly over the top.
Cover the whole tin tightly with a second layer of foil to keep the steam in.
Cook in a 180 C oven for 3 hours, without opening it, until the meat and vegetables are fully tender and the pork falls apart.
Remove the cloths, serve the meat and vegetables together on a platter, and spoon over the cooking juices.

title: Hedgehog slice (no-bake chocolate biscuit slice)

ingredients.name: dark chocolate, melted, for the topping

steps: Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter with the condensed milk and cocoa in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Mix the crushed biscuits, coconut and walnuts into the chocolate mixture.
Press the mixture firmly into the tin.
Spread the melted chocolate over the top and chill for at least 2 hours until set.
Cut into small squares and keep in the fridge.

title: Kiwi onion dip (onion soup and cream dip)

ingredients.name: potato chips and raw vegetables, to serve

steps: Place the sour cream in a bowl, add the cream cheese if using, and stir until smooth.
Stir in the onion soup mix and chives until evenly blended.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the onion powder softens and flavours the cream.
Taste and stir in a little extra soup mix if you want it stronger.
Serve chilled with potato chips and raw vegetables.

title: Lolly cake (no-bake malt biscuit and fruit puff log)

ingredients.name: fruit puffs (soft marshmallow lollies), snipped small

steps: Crush the biscuits into fine crumbs, either in a food processor or in a bag with a rolling pin.
Mix the crumbs with the melted butter and condensed milk until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Stir in the fruit puffs.
Shape the mixture into a log about 6 cm thick on baking paper.
Roll the log in the desiccated coconut until coated, wrap tightly, and chill for at least 4 hours, until firm.
Slice into rounds and serve cold.

title: Louise cake (jam and coconut meringue slice)
steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the egg yolks, then fold in the flour and baking powder to make a soft dough.
Press the dough into the tin and bake for 15 minutes until pale golden.
Spread the jam over the warm base.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff, gradually beat in the caster sugar until glossy, and fold in the coconut. Spread this over the jam.
Bake for another 20 to 25 minutes until the top is crisp and golden, cool in the tin, and cut into squares.

title: Mince and cheese pie (New Zealand meat pie)
steps: Brown the mince with the onion in a pan until no pink remains, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, Worcestershire sauce and tomato sauce, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until very thick. Season and let it cool completely, then stir in the cheese.
Heat the oven to 200 C. Cut the shortcrust pastry into rounds to line four 10 cm pie tins, pressing it in gently.
Fill the pie cases with the cooled filling.
Cut lids from the puff pastry, brush the edges with egg, and press them on, crimping the edges.
Brush the tops with beaten egg and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until deeply golden. Serve with tomato sauce.

title: Mince on toast (savoury beef mince on buttered toast)
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and mince and cook, breaking it up, until well browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste, then add the stock and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy, adding the peas for the last 5 minutes.
Season to taste and spoon generously over the buttered toast.
Serve at once, with a fried egg if you like.

title: Pavlova (meringue nest with cream and fruit)
steps: Heat the oven to 150 C and line a tray with baking paper, drawing a 20 cm circle on it.
Beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until they hold soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoonful at a time, beating well, until the meringue is thick, glossy and no longer gritty.
Fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla.
Pile the meringue onto the circle, shaping it into a round with a slightly hollowed top and swirled sides.

Put it in the oven and immediately reduce the temperature to 120 C. Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until the outside is crisp and pale. Turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely with the door ajar.
Just before serving, top with whipped cream, kiwifruit, strawberries and passionfruit.

title: Rēwena bread (Māori potato-leavened bread)

ingredients.name: medium potato (about 150 g), peeled and grated
plain flour, plus extra for dusting
instant yeast, optional, to speed up the rise

steps: Make the starter ('bug') 2 days ahead: mix the grated potato, 1 tbsp sugar, 250 ml warm water and 2 tbsp flour in a jar, cover loosely, and leave in a warm place for 2 days, stirring once a day, until bubbly and sour-smelling.
Strain the starter, saving the liquid, and discard the potato solids.
Mix the 500 g flour, salt and sugar, then stir in the strained starter liquid, melted butter and enough of the warm water to make a soft dough. Add the optional yeast here if you want a faster rise.
Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth, then cover and rise for 3 to 4 hours, until doubled.
Shape the dough into a loaf or put it in a greased tin and let it rise again for 1 hour.
Bake at 200 C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped. Cool on a rack and serve with butter.
